step1_analysis.description: A bandgap reference circuit that generates a temperature-insensitive voltage using ratioed transistors biased in strong inversion and the inverse-function technique, eliminating the need for physical resistors.

paper_reference.title: A CMOS Bandgap Reference Without Resistors

sky130_expected.calculation: Bandgap references typically target the silicon bandgap voltage of ~1.12V to 1.2V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Expected to be similar to the paper's reported value as it relies on fundamental silicon properties, though exact value depends on transistor sizing.

sky130_expected.calculation: Paper current = 1.4mW / 3.7V = 378uA. For 1.8V supply in sky130, power = 378uA * 1.8V = 0.68mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Scaled down linearly with supply voltage assuming similar bias currents.

TC_Vref.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage variation over temperature (0 to 70 C)

sky130_expected.calculation: Depends heavily on trimming and exact sizing, but typically in the 5-20mV range for un-trimmed or nominally trimmed circuits.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Expected to be in the same order of magnitude as the paper.

Line_Regulation.description: Variation of reference voltage with supply voltage

sky130_expected.calculation: Typically a few mV per V for standard bandgap references.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard performance metric for voltage references to ensure stability against supply variations.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure nominal Vref, power consumption, temperature coefficient, and line regulation.
